the presence of diabetes is associated with a higher prevalence of thrombus with a high degree of organization in patients with acute STEMI, and that the presence of glycative stress is associated with a lower prevalence of thrombus organization in STEMI patients.

the presence of diabetes mellitus (DM) is associated with an increased incidence of STEMI, and that the presence of DM is associated with a higher incidence of in-hospital complications, a longer hospitalization period, and an increased incidence of death during follow-up.
glycative and oxidative stress, and their biomarkers, are associated with the altered thrombus composition of diabetic patients with ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of diabetes on the composition of thrombi in STEMI and the potential mechanisms of these changes.
the effects of diabetes on the thrombotic process.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that there is a strong association between glycative and oxidative stress in the blood and in the thrombus of diabetic patients with STEMI and that these processes are related to altered thrombus composition.
we have demonstrated that glycative and oxidative stress is associated with altered thrombotic composition in diabetic patients presenting with acute ST-elevation myocardium infarction.
we identified a new mechanism of thrombus formation in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), namely, glycative stress, that is, the reaction between sugars and proteins.
